title: The Hinterland Paradox in South Africa
excerpt: Explore how South Africa's institutional erosion has turned it into a vital "back office" for transnational insurgents. While SANDF soldiers fought M23 rebels in the DRC in 2024, the group's leaders operated freely from Johannesburg, fundraising and coordinating logistics. Even after M23's shift to controlled territories in 2025, networks persist for groups like al-Shabaab and ISIS affiliates, exploiting hawala systems, diaspora communities, and regulatory gaps. Highlighting women's pivotal roles in these operations and the risk of domestic blowback, this analysis warns of South Africa's precarious path and calls for urgent reforms to dismantle these hidden architectures before violence hits home.
